subject: Hosted API: data residency, retention & deletion Q&A (Norwood Systems)
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@dataguard.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@dataguard.com
Date: 2028-06-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Security questionnaire: Hosted API — residency & retention details

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this. We're finishing our vendor review and have a short set of clarifying questions about Redwood's hosted API data residency and retention practices. Can you confirm the following for Norwood Systems' expected usage?

1) Primary region: we will be in us-west — can you confirm you can pin customer data and inference workloads to us-west only?
2) Retention windows: what are the default retention windows for (a) request/response payloads, (b) prefix/KV cache, (c) backups/snapshots, (d) audit logs?
3) Deletion mechanics: if we request data deletion, what APIs/processes are used and what are the expected SLAs for each artifact type (immediate purge vs. background removal)?
4) Legal hold / export: can data be exported for e-discovery and held beyond retention? How do holds interact with deletion requests?
5) Evidence / attestation: what artifacts will you provide to confirm deletion (MD5s, timestamps, signed attestation)?
6) Encryption/localization: are backups and logs encrypted-at-rest and stored within the pinned region only?

We appreciate concise, operational answers and any attachments that can be shared with our InfoSec.

Best,
Alex
Security Engineer
DataGuard / Norwood Systems
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@dataguard.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: Hosted API — residency & retention details

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front, attaching a high-level dataflow diagram (hosted-data-flow.pdf). Marissa (security) has the detailed SLAs below — copying her to confirm.

1) Region pinning: yes — hosted tenants can be pinned to us-west (region locking policy). Service endpoints and data stores will remain in us-west unless you request cross-region failover.

2) Default retention (summary):
  • request/response payloads: 30 days (default)
  • KV/prefix cache: ephemeral — typically 0–1 hour depending on workload; cache persistence for optimization only, not a canonical store
  • backups/snapshots: weekly snapshots retained for 90 days by default
  • audit logs: 365 days (retained for security/forensics)

3) Deletions: we offer a programmatic Deletion API for tenant-level and object-level deletes. Immediate token and primary-store metadata purge occurs within 48 hours; snapshot/backup eviction is scheduled and completed within 30 days (we provide a deletion attestation once complete).

4) Legal hold/export: exports for e-discovery are supported via an on-demand export process; holds suspend retention/eviction for affected records until release (we'll surface hold state to customers and pause automated deletion).

5) Attestation: we'll provide a signed deletion attestation (PDF) with timestamps and the list of object IDs removed. For automated audits we can provide operation logs and offsets.

6) Encryption/localization: all customer data, backups, and audit logs are encrypted-at-rest (AES-256) and stored in the pinned region (us-west) by default. KMS integration is supported for customer-managed keys.

I'll let Marissa paste the formal answers and example API calls for deletion and retention controls.

Thanks —
Mina
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@dataguard.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: Hosted API — residency & retention details

Alex — adding technical details and example flows below. Attaching SOC2 summary (SOC2-summary.pdf).

Region pinning and isolation
- Tenant isolation: each customer tenant is logically isolated; storage buckets and compute for pinned tenants are located in the chosen region (us-west). Cross-region replication is opt-in and disabled by default.
- Network controls: VPC peering and private link options available for Dedicated/Private; hosted uses private subnets per region with strict egress rules.

Default retention & technical details (configurable per-tenant)
- Request/response payloads:
  • Default TTL: 30 days.
  • Storage class: short-term object store with lifecycle policy.
  • Rationale: balancing debugability/quality/regression detection vs. exposure.
- KV / prefix cache:
  • Ephemeral caches live in-memory or local NVMe and are not part of canonical backups. Typical TTL is request-driven (0–1 hour), but customers can request a zero-cache policy for sensitive workloads.
- Backups / snapshots:
  • Frequency: weekly logical backups of model-serving state and tenant metadata.
  • Retention: default 90 days; can be shortened or extended with a contract.
- Audit logs:
  • Retention: 365 days default. Logs include request IDs, responding model variant, routing decisions, and metadata (no PII unless supplied in the request payload).

Deletion mechanics & SLAs
- Immediate actions (within 48 hours): primary store objects, request logs indexed for retrieval, and API-accessible items are removed from active stores. We mark deleted objects and purge references from index services.
- Snapshot/backups eviction (within 30 days): background job evicts relevant objects from backups/snapshots per lifecycle.
- Long-tail artifacts (rare): cached KVs, ephemeral GPU caches, or on-disk temp files are garbage-collected within 7 days; if you require certified immediate destruction we can schedule an accelerated purge (expedited deletion for enterprise contracts).

Deletion API (example)
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion-requests - Body: { "type": "tenant", "reason": "customer_requested", "hold_ids": [] }
- Response: 202 Accepted; includes operation_id. Use GET /v1/operations/{operation_id} to track progress (states: queued -> in_progress -> completed).

Attestation & evidence
- When deletion completes we provide:
  • signed PDF attestation with operation_id and timestamp
  • CSV of object IDs removed (if requested)
  • internal audit log snapshot (redacted) showing the purge workflow steps

Legal hold interplay
- Legal holds: when a legal hold is asserted, automated eviction is paused for the scope of the hold. Deletion requests for objects under hold will be queued but not executed until the hold is released. We provide APIs to create/release holds and an audit stream of hold changes.

Encryption & key management
- All-at-rest using AES-256; TLS 1.3 in transit. Customer-managed KMS is supported; with CMK, key rotation and key deletion policies are respected and audited.

Operational notes & timelines (summary)
- Primary purge: <= 48 hours
- Snapshot eviction: <= 30 days
- Ephemeral caches garbage collection: <= 7 days (typically < 24 hours)
- Attestation delivery: within 5 business days after completion

If Norwood wants, we can include a sample deletion operation run in a staging tenant and generate a sample attestation for your legal team. Happy to schedule a short call to walk through the export API.

-Marissa
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Appreciate it —
